title: Article 132 — Appellate jurisdiction of Supreme Court in appeals from High Courts in certain cases

content.overview: Article 132 provides for appeal to the Supreme Court from any judgment, decree or final order of a High Court in the territory of India, whether in a civil, criminal or other proceeding, if the High Court certifies under Article 134A that the case involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution. Where such a certificate is given, any party may appeal on the ground that the question has been wrongly decided, and with leave of the Supreme Court on any other ground.
content.glance: Appeal to SC from HC if HC certifies substantial question of law as to interpretation of the Constitution (Art 134A certificate).
content.study:
Article 132 constitutional appeals:
- From judgment, decree or final order of a High Court (civil, criminal or other).
- Condition: High Court certifies under Article 134A that the case involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution.
- Appeal lies on the ground that such question was wrongly decided; and with SC leave on any other ground.

Examination: constitutional interpretation certificate; substantial question of law; Art 134A link; contrast Arts 133 (civil) and 134 (criminal).

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Appeal from HC judgment/decree/final order (any proceeding).
2. HC certificate under Art 134A: substantial question of law as to interpretation of the Constitution.
3. Appeal on that ground; with SC leave on any other ground.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When does an appeal lie to the Supreme Court under Article 132?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 132, an appeal lies to the Supreme Court from any judgment, decree or final order of a High Court in the territory of India in a civil, criminal or other proceeding if the High Court certifies under Article 134A that the case involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution. The appeal may be on the ground that such question has been wrongly decided and, with the leave of the Supreme Court, on any other ground.

examTips: Constitutional interpretation certificate from HC; substantial question of law.

keyTakeaways: Art 132: appellate jurisdiction on substantial constitutional questions certified by HC.
